Well, affect my job? No, I wouldn't say it stops me from working or doing my shifts. I still go in, I still do my safety trainings. And I still do my volunteering on the weekends. Normal to other people? Oh, I suppose it's possible. I mean, Gary hasn't said anything about it, and he notices everything. Like last week, he noticed I was using the blue pens instead of the black ones on the inventory sheets. The company policy says we're supposed to use black ink for all official documentation, which I think is a bit silly, really. Blue ink is just as easy to read, don't you think? And honestly, the blue pens we get from the supply closet just write so much smoother. The black ones always skip, and then you have to scribble on a piece of scrap paper to get the ink flowing again. 

I keep a little notepad right by my station just for that. It's one of those promotional notepads from a local realtor. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, gave it to me. She just sold her house last month. Moved down to Florida to be closer to her daughter. She had this beautiful garden in her backyard—rose bushes all along the fence, and these huge hydrangeas. I always told her she should enter them in the county fair, but she said it was too much fuss. Now the new owners have moved in, and I swear, they haven't watered those hydrangeas once. It just breaks my heart to see them wilting. I was half tempted to sneak over there with my watering can the other evening, but I didn't want them to think I was some crazy old lady snooping around their yard in the dark. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, my hands and face looking normal to other people. Yeah, I guess maybe they could look fine to someone else. I don't know for sure, because no one's ever brought it up, but it's possible they just don't see what I see.

Could my face ever look not crooked to me? I don't know, I'm not really sure if I'm certain about it. I don't know if you can ever be completely certain about anything, really. You think things are going to stay one way and then they just change out of nowhere. Like the bus schedule. They completely changed the routes for the 42 line last week and didn't put up a single sign at the shelter. I was standing out there for forty-five minutes on Tuesday morning. It was freezing, too! We had that frost advisory, and the wind was just whipping right through my coat. 

My sister, the one I mentioned who came over for the pizza, she keeps telling me to buy one of those heavy down coats from Macy's. But they are just so expensive now. I saw one in their Sunday circular that was almost two hundred dollars. Who pays two hundred dollars for a coat just to stand at the bus stop? She used to sew all her own clothes. She had this big heavy Singer sewing machine, the kind built right into the wooden table with the cast-iron pedal on the bottom. I used to love watching the needle go up and down so fast. 

But, oh dear, I'm rambling again. I'm sorry. What were you asking me? Oh, right, if I'm certain it'll always look crooked to me. I really couldn't tell you. I guess I'm not completely certain, I just don't know. Right now, that's just what I see when I look in the mirror, but I suppose I don't know for sure what the future holds.

Affected my relationships? Well, I still see people. I mean, it hasn't stopped me from working or doing my volunteer shifts at the library. Well, like I said, I haven't stopped working or volunteering, but... I have noticed I'm a lot slower getting ready for things. And I definitely find myself hesitating before social events that I used to enjoy so easily. Like my niece's birthday dinner last weekend... I almost didn't go. The lady who runs the shelter, Susan, she says he’s probably got some Jack Russell in him, which makes sense because he has so much energy. Susan’s been running that place for fifteen years. She actually used to be a dental hygienist before she opened the rescue. Can you imagine? Going from cleaning teeth to cleaning up after dogs all day. But she loves it. They’ve been doing road work on the overpass since last spring and it's just a mess. I try to take the back roads when I can, past the old drive-in theater. And with my hands looking so old and wrinkly when I'm doing the safety manuals... it's just hard to believe people aren't staring at it all, even if they won't admit it.\n\nDoctor: Have your thoughts about your face and hands being crooked and wrinkly changed at all since you first noticed them?\n\nPatient: Changed? Um... no, not really. It’s pretty much just been exactly the same since I first noticed it. It’s a cork board, but they painted the frame this absolute awful shade of yellow. Mustard yellow, really. Gary—my supervisor, I mentioned him earlier—he picked the color. Really good chicken salad, too, with the little green grapes cut up in it and some walnuts. Do other people see it? Well... they tell me they don't. That's actually the main reason I came in to see you. Recently they had me start helping out with the safety trainings at the plant, and when I'm up there pointing things out on the diagrams or the machines, I just can't seem to stop noticing how horribly wrinkly and uneven my hands look. And then they put my picture in the company newsletter, and my face looks completely crooked to me. But when I mention it, the other girls say they don't see it at all.

It used to be a nice, thick matte finish, but now it's this cheap glossy stuff that leaves fingerprint smudges everywhere if you even just hold it. It reminds me of the Sunday newspaper back in the nineties. My husband would sit in his recliner reading the sports section, and his fingers would just be coated in black ink. I had to buy that heavy-duty orange pumice soap just to get his hands clean before church. You know, the kind mechanics use? It smelled so strongly of artificial oranges, it would make my nose itch just walking past the bathroom sink. We used to keep it in this little ceramic dish that my daughter made in her middle school art class. It was supposed to be a turtle, I think, but the glaze melted funny in the kiln...

Oh, for Pete's sake. Look at me, talking about orange soap and ceramic turtles. I am so sorry, my brain just takes a left turn and keeps driving. You asked if anyone else sees what I see.
